articles.title: 完形填空 · 单一绩效目标为何会扭曲行为
articles.context: 文章用伦敦公交和航空公司说明：只考核一个指标会诱发行为扭曲和意外后果，好的目标体系应同时考虑时间、成本、质量和反馈等多个维度。
rows: It's not difficult to set targets for staff.
为员工设定目标并不难。
advance
It is much harder, however, to understand their negative consequences.
然而，更难的是理解这些目标可能带来的负面后果。
contrast
Most work-related behaviors have multiple components.
大多数与工作有关的行为都包含多个组成部分。
explain
Emphasize one and the others become distorted.
过分强调其中一个，其他部分就会被扭曲。
warning
Travel on a London bus and you'll quickly see how this works with drivers.
坐一次伦敦公交，你很快就会看到这种机制如何影响司机。
example
Watch people get on and show their tickets.
看看乘客上车并出示车票的情形。
explain
Are they carefully inspected?
车票会被仔细检查吗？
ask
Never.
从来不会。
emphasize
Do people get on without paying?
有人不付钱就上车吗？
ask
Of course!
当然有！
emphasize
Are there inspectors to check that people have paid?
有没有检查员核查乘客是否付了车费？
ask
Possibly, but very few.
也许有，但少得可怜。
qualify
And people who run for the bus?
那追着公交车跑的人呢？
ask
They are ignored.
他们会被忽视。
emphasize
How about jumping lights?
闯红灯又怎样？
ask
Buses do so almost as frequently as cyclists.
公交车闯红灯的频率几乎和骑车人一样高。
report
Why?
为什么？
ask
Because the target is punctuality.
因为考核目标是准时。
explain
People complained that buses were late and infrequent.
人们曾抱怨公交车迟到、班次太少。
report
So, the number of buses and bus lanes were increased, and drivers were rewarded or punished according to the time they took.
因此，公交车和公交专用道增加了，司机则根据用时受到奖励或惩罚。
sequence
And drivers hit their targets.
于是司机达成了目标。
conclude
But they also hit cyclists.
但他们也撞上了骑车人。
contrast
If the target was changed to revenue, you would have more inspectors and more sensitive pricing.
如果把目标改成营收，就会有更多检查员和更灵敏的定价机制。
example
If the criterion changed to safety, you would get more cautious drivers who obeyed traffic laws.
如果标准改成安全，就会得到更多谨慎、遵守交通法规的司机。
example
But both these criteria would be at the expense of time.
但这两种标准都会以时间为代价。
contrast
There is another problem: people became immensely inventive in hitting targets.
还有一个问题：为了完成目标，人们会变得极其“有创造力”。
advance
Have you noticed that you can leave on a flight an hour late but still arrive on time?
你有没有注意到，飞机晚起飞一小时，却仍可能准时到达？
ask
Tail winds?
是顺风吗？
ask
Of course not!
当然不是！
emphasize
Airlines have simply changed the time a trip is meant to take.
航空公司只是改变了一趟航程名义上应该花费的时间。
explain
A one-hour flight is now billed as a two-hour flight.
原本一小时的航班，如今会被标成两小时。
example
The moral of the story is simple.
这个故事的寓意很简单。
conclude
Most jobs are multidimensional, with multiple criteria.
大多数工作都是多维的，需要多个标准来衡量。
explain
Choose one criterion and you may well sacrifice others.
只选择一个标准，你很可能就会牺牲其他标准。
warning
Everything can be done faster and made cheaper, but there is a cost.
任何事情都可以做得更快、更便宜，但总要付出代价。
contrast
Setting targets can and does have unforeseen negative consequences.
设定目标可能、而且确实会带来意料之外的负面后果。
conclude
This is not an argument against target-setting.
这并不是反对设定目标。
qualify
But it is an argument for exploring consequences first.
而是主张先弄清目标可能产生的后果。
contrast
All good targets should have multiple criteria accounting for critical factors such as time, money, quality and customer feedback.
所有好的目标都应包含多个标准，把时间、金钱、质量和客户反馈等关键因素计算在内。
explain
The trick is not to specify just one or even two dimensions of the objective, but also to understand how to help people better achieve the objective.
关键不是只规定目标的一个甚至两个维度，而是还要理解怎样帮助人们更好地实现整体目标。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 1 · 疫情时代的再培训与技能错配
articles.context: 文章讨论快速变化的技能需求、再培训由谁买单，以及疫情中瑞典航空把停岗乘务员短训后转去支援医院的案例。
rows: “Reskilling” is something that sounds like a buzzword but is actually a requirement if we plan to have a future in which a lot of would-be workers do not get left behind.
“再培训”听起来像一个流行词，但如果我们希望未来大量潜在劳动者不被落下，它实际上是必需的。
advance
We know we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will change rapidly, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain.
我们知道，未来需求旺盛的岗位会迅速变化，保留下来的岗位对技能的要求也会随之改变。
explain
Research by the World Economic Forum finds that on average 42 per cent of the “core skills” within job roles will change by 2022.
世界经济论坛的研究发现，到2022年，各类岗位平均有42%的“核心技能”将发生变化。
statistic
That is a very short timeline.
这个时间窗口非常短。
emphasize
The question of who should pay for reskilling is a thorny one.
谁应为再培训买单，是一个棘手的问题。
advance
For individual companies, the temptation is always to let go of workers whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are.
对单个企业而言，最诱人的做法往往是解雇技能不再需要的员工，再换上技能符合需求的人。
explain
That does not always happen.
但事情并不总是如此。
contrast
AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company that decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy.
AT&T常被视为典范：它选择大规模再培训，而不是采取“解雇再招聘”的策略。
example
Other companies had also pledged to create their own plans.
其他公司也承诺制定自己的计划。
report
When the skills mismatch is in the broader economy, though, the focus usually turns to government to handle.
不过，当技能错配发生在更广泛的经济层面时，人们通常会把解决责任转向政府。
contrast

Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high.
加拿大等地的努力充其量只能说相当迟缓，于是我们常常听到雇主苦苦寻找工人，哪怕在失业率很高的时期和地区也是如此。
warning
With the pandemic, unemployment is very high indeed.
疫情之下，失业率确实非常高。
advance
In February, at 3.5 per cent and 5.5 per cent respectively, unemployment rates in Canada and the United States were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere.
2月时，加拿大和美国失业率分别为3.5%和5.5%，处于一代人以来的低位，各地都在缺人。
statistic
As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 per cent and 13.7 per cent, and although many worker shortages had disappeared, not all had done so.
到5月，这两个数字飙升到13.3%和13.7%；虽然许多岗位短缺消失了，但并非全部。
contrast
In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel.
以医疗领域这个明显例子来说，疫情意味着医生、护士和其他医务人员仍然明显短缺。
example
Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks.
当然，你不可能把一名失业服务员在几周内培训成医生。
qualify
But even if you cannot close that gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned.
但即使填不上这个缺口，也许可以填补其他缺口，而这样做会让所有相关方受益。
contrast

That seems to be the case in Sweden: When forced to furlough 90 per cent of their cabin staffs Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff.
瑞典似乎就是如此：斯堪的纳维亚航空被迫暂时解雇90%的乘务人员后，启动了一项短期再培训计划，让这些停岗员工转而支援医院人员。
example
The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university.
这项行动是集体合作的结果，既有其他企业参与，也有一所瑞典大学参与。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 2 · 英国粮食自给真的可行吗
articles.context: 文章评估脱欧背景下英国提高粮食自给率的主张，指出土地、气候、畜牧结构和耕地比例决定了完全自给并不现实。
rows: With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050, and forecasts that agricultural production in some regions will need to nearly double to keep pace, food security is increasingly making headlines.
预计到2050年全球人口将接近100亿，一些地区的农业产量需要接近翻番才能跟上需求，因此粮食安全越来越受到关注。
advance
In the UK, it has become a big talking point recently too, for a rather particular reason: Brexit.
在英国，粮食安全最近也成为热门话题，原因很特别：脱欧。
explain
Brexit is seen by some as an opportunity to reverse a recent trend towards the UK importing food.
一些人把脱欧视为扭转英国近年来食品进口趋势的机会。
report
The country produces only about 60 per cent of the food it eats, down from almost three-quarters in the late 1980s.
英国目前只生产本国消费食品的大约60%，低于20世纪80年代末接近四分之三的水平。
statistic
A move back to self-sufficiency, the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation's health.
这种观点认为，重新走向自给自足会促进农业、政治主权，甚至改善国民健康。
explain
Sounds great—but how feasible is this vision?
听起来很美好——但这种愿景究竟有多可行？
ask
According to a report on UK food production from the University of Leeds, UK, 85 per cent of the country's total land area is associated with meat and dairy production.
英国利兹大学一份关于本国食品生产的报告称，全国85%的土地面积与肉类和乳制品生产有关。
report
That supplies 80 per cent of what is consumed, so even covering the whole country in livestock farms wouldn't allow us to cover all our meat and dairy needs.
这些土地供应了消费量的80%，因此即使把全国都变成畜牧场，也无法满足全部肉类和乳制品需求。
conclude
There are many caveats to those figures, but they are still grave.
这些数字有许多限制条件，但情况依然严峻。
qualify

To become much more self-sufficient, the UK would need to drastically reduce its consumption of animal foods, and probably also farm more intensively—meaning fewer green fields and more factory-style production.
要显著提高自给率，英国就必须大幅减少动物性食品消费，也可能需要更集约地耕作——这意味着更少的绿色田野和更多工厂化生产。
warning
But switching to a mainly plant-based diet wouldn't help.
但改成以植物为主的饮食也无济于事。
contrast
There is a good reason why the UK is dominated by animal husbandry: most of its terrain doesn't have the right soil or climate to grow crops on a commercial basis.
英国以畜牧业为主有充分理由：大部分地区的土壤或气候并不适合商业化种植农作物。
explain
Just 25 per cent of the country's land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields.
全国只有25%的土地适合种植作物，而且其中大部分已经是耕地。
statistic

Even if we converted all the suitable land to fields of fruit and veg—which would involve taking out all the nature reserves and removing thousands of people from their homes—we would achieve only a 30 per cent boost in crop production.
即使把所有适宜土地都改成果蔬田——这将意味着取消所有自然保护区并让数千人搬离家园——作物产量也只能提高30%。
statistic
Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown, so even with the most extreme measures we could meet only 30 per cent of our fresh produce needs.
目前英国消费的果蔬只有23%是本土生产，因此即便采取最极端措施，也只能满足30%的新鲜农产品需求。
statistic
That is before we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake.
这还没有考虑要从哪里腾出土地，去种植构成我们当前绝大部分热量来源的谷物、糖料、种子和油料作物。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 3 · 科技巨头“小额收购”的竞争争议
articles.context: 文章围绕微软收购Wunderlist和Sunrise展开，讨论大型科技公司通过小额收购吸纳人才乃至提前消灭潜在竞争者的争议，以及美国监管机构开始调查。
rows: When Microsoft bought task management app Wunderlist and mobile calendar Sunrise in 2015, it picked two newcomers that were attracting considerable buzz in Silicon Valley.
2015年微软收购任务管理应用Wunderlist和移动日历Sunrise时，选中的是两家在硅谷颇受关注的新秀。
story
Microsoft's own Office dominates the market for “productivity” software, but the start-ups represented a new wave of technology designed from the ground up for the smartphone world.
微软自己的Office主导“生产力”软件市场，但这两家初创公司代表了从一开始就为智能手机世界设计的新一代技术。
contrast
Both apps, however, were later scrapped after Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products.
然而，这两款应用后来都被停止，因为微软称已把它们最好的功能用于自己的产品。
contrast
Their teams of engineers stayed on, making them two of the many “acqui-hires” that the biggest companies have used to feed their great hunger for tech talent.
但工程师团队留了下来，这使它们成为大型公司为满足技术人才需求而进行的众多“收购式招聘”中的两个案例。
explain
To Microsoft's critics, the fates of Wunderlist and Sunrise are examples of a remorseless drive by Big Tech to chew up any innovative companies that lie in their path.
在微软的批评者看来，Wunderlist和Sunrise的命运体现了科技巨头无情吞噬挡在路上的创新公司的冲动。
warning
“They bought the seedlings and closed them down,” complained Paul Arnold, a partner at San Francisco-based Switch Ventures, putting an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors.
旧金山Switch Ventures合伙人保罗·阿诺德抱怨说：“他们买下幼苗，然后把它们关掉。”这等于终结了那些有朝一日可能成长为竞争者的企业。
dialogue
Microsoft declined to comment.
微软拒绝置评。
report
Like other start-up investors, Mr Arnold's own business often depends on selling start-ups to larger tech companies, though he admits to mixed feelings about the result.
和其他初创投资者一样，阿诺德自己的生意也常依赖把初创公司卖给更大的科技企业，不过他承认自己对此感受复杂。
qualify
“I think these things are good for me, if I put my selfish hat on.
“如果我只从自己的利益出发，我认为这些事对我是有好处的。
dialogue
But are they good for the American economy?
但它们对美国经济有好处吗？
ask
I don't know.”
我不知道。”
dialogue
The U.S. Federal Trade Commission says it wants to find the answer to that question.
美国联邦贸易委员会表示，希望找到这个问题的答案。
advance
This week, it asked the five most valuable U.S. tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions over the past decade.
本周，该机构要求美国市值最高的五家科技公司提供过去十年众多小额收购的信息。
report
Although only a research project at this stage, the request has raised the prospect of regulators wading into early-stage tech markets that until now have been beyond their reach.
尽管目前只是研究项目，这项要求已经使监管机构未来介入此前难以触及的早期科技市场成为可能。
conclude
Given their combined market value of more than $5.5 trillion, rifling through such small deals—many of them much less prominent than Wunderlist and Sunrise—might seem beside the point.
考虑到这五家公司合计市值超过5.5万亿美元，翻查这类小额交易——其中许多远不如Wunderlist和Sunrise知名——似乎有些抓错重点。
qualify

Between them, the five biggest tech companies have spent an average of only $3.4 billion a year on sub-$1 billion acquisitions over the past five years—a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves, and the more than $130 billion of venture capital that was invested in the U.S. last year.
过去五年，这五大科技公司每年用于10亿美元以下收购的平均支出只有34亿美元；与其庞大资金储备及去年美国超过1300亿美元的风险投资相比，这只是沧海一粟。
statistic

However, critics say the big companies use such deals to buy their most threatening potential competitors before their businesses have a chance to gain momentum, in some cases as part of a “buy and kill” tactic to simply close them down.
然而批评者称，大公司会利用这类交易，在最具威胁的潜在竞争者尚未发展起来之前就将其收购；有时这甚至属于“买下并杀死”的策略，目的就是直接关闭它们。
warning

articles.title: 阅读 Text 4 · 复杂社会判断中直觉何时胜过深思
articles.context: 文章介绍“薄片判断”研究：在某些复杂社会判断和偏好形成中，过度分析会让人被显眼细节误导，而直觉整合大量细微信号反而更准确；但直觉并非适用于所有任务。
rows: We're fairly good at judging people based on first impressions, thin slices of experience ranging from a glimpse of a photo to a five-minute interaction, and deliberation can be not only extraneous but intrusive.
我们相当擅长根据第一印象判断他人，这种经验“薄片”可以短到一瞥照片、长到五分钟互动；而深思有时不仅多余，甚至会形成干扰。
advance

In one study of the ability she called “thin slicing,” the late psychologist Nalini Ambady asked participants to watch silent 10-second video clips of professors and to rate the instructor's overall effectiveness.
已故心理学家纳利尼·安巴迪把这种能力称为“薄片判断”；在一项研究中，她让参与者观看教授的10秒无声视频，并评价教师的整体教学效果。
report
Their ratings correlated strongly with students' end-of-semester ratings.
他们的评分与学生在学期末给出的评分高度相关。
report
Another set of participants had to count backward from 1,000 by nines as they watched the clips, occupying their conscious working memory.
另一组参与者观看视频时还必须从1000开始每次减9倒数，以占用其有意识的工作记忆。
sequence
Their ratings were just as accurate, demonstrating the intuitive nature of the social processing.
他们的评分同样准确，这表明这种社会信息加工本质上具有直觉性。
conclude
Critically, another group was asked to spend a minute writing down reasons for their judgment, before giving the rating.
关键是，另一组人在评分前被要求花一分钟写下作出判断的理由。
advance
Accuracy dropped dramatically.
结果准确率大幅下降。
emphasize

Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression.
安巴迪怀疑，深思让他们把注意力集中在某些鲜明却可能误导的线索上，例如特定手势或话语，而没有让各种细微信号复杂互动并形成整体印象。
explain
She found similar interference when participants watched 15-second clips of pairs of people and judged whether they were strangers, friends, or dating partners.
当参与者观看两人相处的15秒视频，并判断他们是陌生人、朋友还是情侣时，她也发现了类似干扰。
example
Other research shows we're better at detecting deception from thin slices when we rely on intuition instead of reflection.
其他研究表明，在依据短暂片段识别欺骗时，依赖直觉而不是反思会让我们表现得更好。
report
“It's as if you're driving a stick shift,” says Judith Hall, a psychologist at Northeastern University.
东北大学心理学家朱迪思·霍尔说：“这就像你在开手动挡汽车。
dialogue
“And if you start thinking about it too much, you can't remember what you're doing.
“一旦开始想得太多，你反而记不起自己正在做什么。
dialogue
But if you go on automatic pilot, you're fine.
但如果进入自动驾驶般的状态，就没问题。
dialogue
Much of our social life is like that.”
我们的很多社会生活也是如此。”
dialogue
Thinking too much can also harm our ability to form preferences.
想得太多还会损害我们形成偏好的能力。
advance
College students' ratings of strawberry jams and college courses aligned better with experts' opinions when the students weren't asked to analyze their rationale.
当大学生没有被要求分析理由时，他们对草莓酱和大学课程的评分反而与专家意见更一致。
report

And people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex—when they had a lot of information to process.
当人们被要求关注感受而非细节时，购车决定在客观上更好、主观上也更满意，但这只发生在决策复杂、需要处理大量信息时。
qualify
Intuition's special powers are unleashed only in certain circumstances.
直觉的特殊力量只会在特定情境下释放。
warning

In one study, participants completed a battery of eight tasks, including four that tapped reflective thinking (discerning rules, comprehending vocabulary) and four that tapped intuition and creativity (generating new products or figures of speech).
一项研究让参与者完成八项任务，其中四项考查反思性思维（辨别规则、理解词汇），另外四项考查直觉和创造力（产生新产品创意或修辞表达）。
report
Then they rated the degree to which they had used intuition (“gut feelings,” “hunches,” “my heart”).
随后，他们评价自己使用直觉——“本能感觉”“预感”“我的内心”——的程度。
sequence
Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks, as expected, and helped them on the rest.
正如预期，依赖直觉损害了他们在前四项任务中的表现，却帮助了他们完成其余任务。
contrast
Sometimes the heart is smarter than the head.
有时候，内心确实比头脑更聪明。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Part B · 如何与权力比你大的人表达不同意见
articles.context: 文章给出向上级表达反对意见的五步法：判断时机、找共同目标、先征求同意、保持冷静、保持谦逊并把观点表述成可被讨论的意见。
rows: Your boss proposes a new initiative you think won't work.
老板提出一项你认为行不通的新举措。
story
Your senior colleague outlines a project timeline you believe is unrealistic.
资深同事提出一个你认为不现实的项目时间表。
story
What do you say when you disagree with someone who has more power than you do?
当你不同意一个比你更有权力的人时，该怎么说？
ask
How do you decide whether it's worth speaking up?
你如何判断这件事是否值得开口？
ask
And if you do, what exactly should you say?
如果决定说，又究竟该说什么？
ask
Here's how to disagree with someone more powerful than you.
下面就是与权力高于你的人表达不同意见的方法。
advance
You may decide it's best to hold off on voicing your opinion.
你可能会决定暂时不表达意见更好。
qualify
Maybe you haven't finished thinking the problem through, or you want to get a clearer sense of what the group thinks.
也许你还没有把问题想透，或者想先更清楚地了解团队的看法。
explain
If you think other people are going to disagree, too, you might want to gather your army first.
如果你认为其他人也会反对，也许可以先争取支持者。
example
People can contribute experience or information to your thinking—all the things that would make the disagreement stronger or more valid.
别人可以为你的思考补充经验或信息，这些都会让你的反对意见更有力、更站得住脚。
explain
It's also a good idea to delay the conversation if you're in a meeting or other public space.
如果当时在会议或其他公共场合，推迟这场谈话也是好主意。
explain
Discussing the issue in private will make the powerful person feel less threatened.
私下讨论会让权力较大的一方感到没那么受威胁。
conclude
Before you share your thoughts, think about what the powerful person cares about—it may be the credibility of their team or getting a project done on time.
在表达想法前，先想想对方最在意什么——可能是团队的可信度，也可能是项目按时完成。
advance
You're more likely to be heard if you can connect your disagreement to a higher purpose.
如果能把不同意见与更高层次的目标联系起来，你更可能被听进去。
explain
State it overtly, contextualizing your statements so that you're seen not as a disagreeable subordinate but as a colleague who's trying to advance a common objective.
把这个共同目标明确说出来，并为自己的话提供背景，让你看起来不是一个难相处的下属，而是努力推动共同目标的同事。
explain
The discussion will then become more like a chess game than a boxing match.
这样，讨论就更像一盘棋，而不是一场拳击赛。
conclude
This step may sound overly deferential, but it's a smart way to give the powerful person psychological safety and control.
这一步听起来可能过分恭敬，但它能聪明地给对方心理安全感和控制感。
qualify
You can say something like, “I know we seem to be moving toward a first-quarter commitment here—I have reasons to think that won't work, I'd like to lay out my reasoning. Would that be OK?”
你可以这样说：“我知道我们似乎正准备承诺第一季度完成——但我有理由认为这行不通，我想把理由说明一下，可以吗？”
dialogue
This gives the person a choice, allowing him to verbally opt in.
这给了对方选择权，让他可以口头同意继续讨论。
explain
And, assuming he says yes, it will make you feel more confident about voicing your disagreement.
而一旦他答应，你表达不同意见时也会更有信心。
conclude
You might feel your heart racing or your face turning red, but do whatever you can to remain neutral in both your words and actions.
你可能会心跳加速、脸色发红，但要尽一切可能让言语和举止保持中性。
warning
When your body language communicates reluctance or anxiety, it undercuts the message.
当肢体语言传达出犹豫或焦虑时，它会削弱你说出的信息。
explain
It sends a mixed message, and your counterpart gets to choose what signals to read.
这会发出相互矛盾的信号，而对方可以自行选择相信哪一个。
explain
Deep breaths can help, as can speaking more slowly and deliberately.
深呼吸有帮助，放慢语速并更从容地说话也有帮助。
encourage
When we feel panicky, we tend to talk louder and faster.
人在慌张时往往会说得更响、更快。
explain
Simply slowing the pace and talking in an even tone helps the other person cool down and does the same for you.
只要放慢节奏、保持平稳语调，就能帮助对方冷静下来，也能让你自己冷静。
resolve
It also makes you seem confident, even if you aren't.
即使你内心并不自信，这样做也会让你看起来更有把握。
conclude
Emphasize that you're only offering your opinion, not gospel truth.
强调你只是提出自己的观点，而不是宣告绝对真理。
advance
It may be a well-informed, well-researched opinion, but it's still an opinion, so talk tentatively and slightly understate your confidence.
这个观点也许信息充分、研究扎实，但仍只是观点，因此要以试探的口吻表达，并稍微降低自信程度。
qualify
Instead of saying, “If we set an end-of-quarter deadline, we'll never make it,” say, “This is just my opinion, but I don't see how we will make that deadline.”
不要说“如果把截止日期定在季度末，我们绝对完不成”，而可以说“这只是我的看法，但我还看不出我们怎样能赶上这个期限”。
example
Having asserted your position (as a position, not as a fact), demonstrate equal curiosity about other views.
在表明自己的立场——注意，是立场而不是事实——之后，也要对其他观点表现出同等的好奇。
explain
Remind the person that this is your point of view, and then invite critique.
提醒对方这只是你的观点，然后邀请他批评指正。
encourage
Be open to hearing other opinions.
对其他意见保持开放。
conclude

articles.title: 翻译 · 陌生人的短暂交流也能提升归属感
articles.context: 文章介绍研究发现：与陌生人交谈往往会改善情绪与归属感，而人们之所以回避，常是误以为陌生人不愿交流。
rows: We tend to think that friends and family members are our biggest sources of connection, laughter, and warmth.
我们往往认为，朋友和家人是我们获得联结、欢笑与温暖的最大来源。
advance
While that may well be true, researchers have also recently found that interacting with strangers actually brings a boost in mood and feelings of belonging that we didn't expect.
这很可能确实如此，但研究人员最近还发现，与陌生人互动实际上会带来我们未曾预料的情绪改善和归属感提升。
contrast
In one series of studies, researchers instructed Chicago-area commuters using public transportation to strike up a conversation with someone near them.
在一系列研究中，研究人员让芝加哥地区乘坐公共交通的通勤者主动与身边的人交谈。
report
On average, participants who followed this instruction felt better than those who had been told to stand or sit in silence.
平均而言，照做的参与者比那些被要求默默站着或坐着的人感觉更好。
compare
The researchers also argued that when we shy away from casual interactions with strangers, it is often due to a misplaced anxiety that they might not want to talk to us.
研究人员还认为，我们之所以回避与陌生人的随意交流，往往源于一种错位的焦虑：担心对方不愿和我们说话。
explain
Much of the time, however, this belief is false.
然而很多时候，这种想法并不正确。
contrast
As it turns out, many people are actually perfectly willing to talk—and may even be flattered to receive your attention.
事实证明，许多人其实非常愿意交谈，甚至可能因为得到你的关注而感到受宠若惊。
conclude
